published_statement: Thm 1.2 (p. 11): 'For any choice of past-compact smooth tensor S_ab(x) and for any symmetric past-compact smooth function Xi(x,y), there exists unique past-compact solution (omega~_1, h~_ab) of the Cauchy problem for the linearised semiclassical Einstein-Klein-Gordon equations [system (1.8) with zero data on Sigma_-eps] for any time t in [0, infinity). For any nontrivial choice of the sources S_ab and Xi, the solution h~_ab grows exponentially in time, but it can be bounded from above by the conformal rescaling of the Minkowski metric using a universal factor H, i.e. h~_ab <= e^{-Ht} eta_ab.'  Thm 4.14 (p. 53): 'For a_i in (-infinity, 4m^2) and for any choice of past-compact smooth source S supported in the future of Sigma_-eps, the equation phi + W_ret(phi) = S, which is equivalent to the prototypical semiclassical equation (4.24), admits a unique smooth and past-compact solution phi, supported in the future of Sigma_-eps.'  Prop. 2.4 (p. 19): 'Let h_ab in Gamma_pc(T*R^n (x)_s T*R^n). Then, there is exactly one vector field X~_a in Gamma_pc(T*R^n), which makes the trace-reversal h-bar_ab divergence-free', with X~^T_a = -v-bar^T_a, Y~ = -G_ret((n-1)/(2(n-2)) box w-bar + 1/(2(n-2)) h-bar).
published_hypotheses: background (M, eta) = Minkowski R^4 with the Poincare vacuum omega_0 of ONE real Klein-Gordon field of mass m, coupling xi (sec. 1.2, Prop. 3.1); quasifree Hadamard constraint (I) and global hyperbolicity (II) (sec. 1.2, p. 5)
renormalised <:T_ab:> by the Hollands-Wald axioms, eq. (1.2), with alpha_1 = (1/64 pi^2)(-3/2 + 2 gamma + log(m^2/2 mu^2)) so that (eta, omega_0) solves the system (Prop. 3.1)
forcing problem (1.8): perturbations (h~_ab, omega~_1) in Gamma_pc (x) D'_pc(M x M), sources S_ab, Xi smooth and past-compact (supported in the future of Sigma_-eps), zero data on Sigma_-eps
de Donder gauge: complete gauge fixing for PAST-COMPACT gauge vectors X_a in Gamma_pc(T*R^n) (Prop. 2.4, Remark 2.6); the formula divides by n - 2
S/TT decoupling (Thm 1.1, (1.10)-(1.11)); each sector cast in the prototype (4.3)/(4.9) with a_1 = a_2 = a: S sector a = 2m^2/(6 xi - 1) (5.1), TT sector a = 4m^2 (5.2)
Thm 4.14 hypothesis: a_i in (-infinity, 4m^2) (OPEN interval); Prop. 4.12 the same; Prop. 4.11 a_i <= 4m^2; Lemma 4.13 uses a_1, a_2, gamma in (-infinity, 4m^2) and claims A'(I) = R
sec. 5.1: 'in order to fulfil the hypotheses of Proposition 4.5, we need to choose xi in such a way that 2/(6 xi - 1) < 4'
NOT hypotheses of well-posedness: alpha~^S_2 = alpha~^TT_2 = 0 and alpha~_1 by Thm 3.6 (sec. 5.1-5.2) fix the physical b_i, but Prop. 4.12 holds 'for every b~_0, b~_1, b~_2 in R'
Thm 1.2 as printed states NO hypothesis on m, xi or the renormalisation constants; they sit in the body (Thm 4.14, sec. 5.1)
hypothesis_drift: SOURCE GAP INHERITED, UNFLAGGED BY THE OWNER (TT sector outside Thm 4.14's stated hypothesis): linstab.py:142 records 'RESULT Thm 1.2 / 4.14: unique past-compact solutions exist' for the whole system, and linstab.py:133 carries the parameter condition only for the S sector ('2/(6 xi - 1) < 4 (5.1, for Prop. 4.5)'). At source the TT sector has a_1 = a_2 = 4m^2 (5.2, p. 60; T = (1/60)(box - 4m^2)^2, raw layout confirmed), which is the EXCLUDED endpoint of Thm 4.14's and Prop. 4.12's hypothesis a_i in (-infinity, 4m^2) [computed C2a-C2b]. GMMPS nonetheless write in 5.2 (p. 62) 'the existence of solutions is provided by Theorem 4.14'. COMPUTED: at a = 4m^2, Lemma 4.13's step lim_{gamma -> 4m^2-} A'(gamma) = +infinity FAILS -- A'(4m^2 - eps) = -6.3e-9 at eps = 1e-6 (m = 1), A' < 0 on all of I, so A'(I) is contained in (-infinity, 0), not R (C3c-C3d); convexity survives (C3e). Hence Prop. 4.12's tangent construction (b_2 = A'(gamma~)) is unavailable for every b_2 >= 0, and for b_2 > 1/(8 pi^2) = 0.012665 (m-independent; = sup_I (A' + gamma A''/2) = 4m^2 J(4m^2), C4pre, C4lim) G(gamma) = gamma A - b_2 gamma^2 is concave on I, so NO auxiliary (b_0, b_1) gives the three real roots in (-infinity, 4m^2) that Thm 4.14's proof uses (L = (box - gamma_0)(box - gamma_1)(box - gamma_2), gamma_i in (-infinity, 4m^2), p. 53) [C4a, grid evidence]. By comparing the printed TT equation (p. 60) with (4.9), b_2 = 120 alpha~^TT_4 (my reading; the paper says only 'proportional'), so the gap covers alpha~^TT_4 > 1/(960 pi^2) = 1.06e-4, which contains GMMPS's own TT regime 'b_2 ... positive and large' (p. 62). This is a gap between a stated hypothesis and its application, NOT a refutation: no ill-posed TT source is exhibited, and Prop. 4.10 also admits a complex-conjugate root pair, a route Thm 4.14's proof (real gamma_i) does not cover.

CONTROL (the S sector IS covered): with a = 2m^2/(6 xi - 1) < 4m^2, e.g. xi = 0, a = -2m^2, Lemma 4.13's divergence is reproduced (A'(4 - eps) ~ eps^-1/2: 14.1 at 1e-5, 44.7 at 1e-6, C3b) and Prop. 4.12's tangent construction yields three real roots in I (b_2 = 0.2, C4b).

IMPLICIT, UNNAMED IN SOURCE AND OWNER: '2/(6 xi - 1) < 4' is equivalent to xi in (-inf, 1/6) U (1/4, inf) (C1a, sympy); xi = 1/6 (conformal coupling) is excluded -- a is undefined and the S operator loses its box^2 term, so the S sector's top-order nonlocal term vanishes (C1b, C1e). The owner copies the condition verbatim (linstab.py:133); the exclusion of xi in [1/6, 1/4] is not spelled out by either.

ATTRIBUTION NUANCE (copied from the source, not an owner drift): GMMPS 5.1 and linstab.py:133 attribute the xi condition to Prop. 4.5; Prop. 4.5's own hypotheses are on the density varsigma (positive, L^2, Holder), and the a-condition enters through Prop. 4.11 (a_i <= 4m^2) and Prop. 4.12 / Thm 4.14 (a_i < 4m^2). The strict '< 4' the owner records matches Thm 4.14.

NOT A DROP: the owner's hypothesis list (linstab.py:305-312, GMMPS_HYPOTHESES) is MORE explicit than Thm 1.2's printed statement, which names none. alpha~_2 = 0 (assumed, 5.1-5.2) is absent from the canonical entry's five hypotheses but present in the owner (linstab.py:311); it is not a hypothesis of well-posedness (Prop. 4.12: 'for every b~_i'), so its absence from the entry changes nothing here.

SCOPE USE CONFIRMED AT SOURCE (linstab.py:88-92, 1051-1052): the forcing problem (1.8) is posed in Gamma_pc(x^2_s T*M) (+) D'_pc(M x M) on Minkowski with the global Poincare vacuum; Prop. 2.4 is on R^n with retarded G_ret over all of R^n; Thm 4.14's operator is built from the 5-D retarded propagator restricted to M and a Fourier-Laplace transform over all p in R^3 (p. 54). A region of Minkowski bounded by a shell satisfies none of these, so FLAT_EXTERIOR_INHERITS_GMMPS = False is supported as READ; the TT gap above only strengthens it.

DISCREPANCIES IN THE SOURCE'S Thm 1.2 NOT USED BY THE TREE (recorded, not refutations): (i) the bound is printed 'h~_ab <= e^{-Ht} eta_ab' for a solution said to grow exponentially; 5.2.1 describes the conformal factor Omega = e^{-Ht} as REMOVING the growth, so the intended bound is presumably e^{-Ht} h~ bounded -- a misprint-level sign discrepancy; (ii) 'for any nontrivial choice of the sources ... grows exponentially' is stronger than Thm 4.16 ('for some ranges of parameters ... solutions are bounded and decay', p. 10/41) and than 5.2's own Planck-mass TT example (m = 1, a = 4, b_1 = 2.5, b_2 = -0.7: zeros 0 and two positive, p. 62); (iii) the data are printed 'h~_ab|Sigma_eps = d_t h~_ab|Sigma_-eps = 0' (Thm 1.2 and (1.9)) against Sigma_-eps in (1.8); (iv) Prop. 4.5 states '1 < c < 4m^2' for a constant of dimension mass^2 (units convention, not an error). The owner quotes only the existence/uniqueness sentence.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for THIS result: Thm 1.2 / 4.14 and Prop. 2.4 are mathematical theorems quantified over every m > 0, kappa > 0 and every b~_i; no measured datum enters, so nothing the authors could have lacked in data can move them (data_at_publication row 1). What the source lacks is not data but a proof for one sector: the TT sector's a = 4m^2 sits at the endpoint Thm 4.14 excludes, and the computation here shows the paper's own route (Lemma 4.13 -> Prop. 4.12 -> real gamma_i in Thm 4.14) cannot reach TT for any b_2 >= 0 by tangency and for any b_2 > 1/(8 pi^2) by any real-root choice. Evidence the other way: the S sector under 2/(6 xi - 1) < 4 is covered and its Lemma 4.13 / Prop. 4.12 steps reproduce here; the gauge fixing (Prop. 2.4) closes identically. So M's suspicion finds no inaccurate datum, but it does find an incomplete step -- a hypothesis/application mismatch in the source -- that the tree inherits without naming. Having it closed (or not) would not change the tree's only dependent verdict, FLAT_EXTERIOR_INHERITS_GMMPS = False, which rests on the posing on all of R^4 and is confirmed as READ.
grade_evidence: The theorem as the tree records it ('unique past-compact solutions exist', linstab.py:142, for the whole S + TT system) is proved at source only on a smaller class: the S sector with a = 2m^2/(6 xi - 1) < 4m^2 (xi < 1/6 or xi > 1/4, C1a), where Lemma 4.13 and Prop. 4.12 reproduce (C3b, C4b). The TT sector has a = 4m^2 (C2a), outside Thm 4.14's own stated hypothesis a_i in (-oo, 4m^2) (C2b); there Lemma 4.13's A'(I) = R fails (A'(I) in (-oo, 0), C3c-d), so the tangent construction is unavailable for b_2 >= 0 and no real three-root choice exists for b_2 > 1/(8 pi^2) (C4lim, C4a), a range that contains GMMPS's own TT regime 'b_2 positive and large' (p. 62). Not WRONG: no counterexample to TT well-posedness is shown, only that the published proof does not reach it. Not DATA-DEPENDENT: no datum enters. The tree's dependent pin FLAT_EXTERIOR_INHERITS_GMMPS = False is unaffected (its basis -- (1.8) posed on all of Minkowski with the global Poincare vacuum and past-compact support, Prop. 2.4 on R^n, Thm 4.14 via Fourier over all of R^3 -- is READ and confirmed). Thm 1.2's second sentence (growth, e^{-Ht} bound) carries misprint-level and scope discrepancies but is not used by the tree.
what_would_change_the_grade: STANDS: a proof (GMMPS v2, an erratum, or arXiv:2507.05004-style extension) of Thm 4.14 at a_i = 4m^2 or with a complex-conjugate pair gamma_1 = conj(gamma_2) from Prop. 4.10, covering b_2 > 0; or a reading showing GMMPS treat TT by a different, already-stated route that this text dump does not show. WRONG (for the TT half only): an explicit past-compact TT source with no past-compact solution, or non-uniqueness, at a = 4m^2. A continuum proof (not a grid) that G'' < 0 on I for b_2 > 1/(8 pi^2) would harden C4a without changing the grade. A live re-read of v1 at alphaXiv would replace the DOCKET-64 dump as the READ route.
